messages:
maria: FYI customer AcmePay opened a high-sev — service endpoint sometimes resolves to public IP from their prod pods, causing TLS cert errors and 503s. Seen since their VPC migration last night.

maria: short repro they gave: from a prod pod in us-east-1 ->
```
# from pod
$ dig +short svc.acmepay-internal.example
54.210.33.12   # sometimes this
10.2.5.18       # sometimes this
```

maria: when it resolves to 54.210.33.12 tls handshake fails because SNI cert is for `*.elb.amazonaws.com` not our internal cert.

alex: @maria can you paste the pod's /etc/resolv.conf and node-local-dns config? also which cluster (eks-prod-3?)

maria: cluster=eks-prod-3, resolv.conf from pod:
```
nameserver 169.254.20.10
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local example
options ndots:5
```

maria: node-local-dns ip is 169.254.20.10, node-local log shows: `failed to forward to 10.0.2.2:53: dial udp 10.0.2.2:53: i/o timeout` then `fallback to 8.8.8.8`

rashid: that log is telling — node-local can't reach VPC resolver (10.0.2.2). If it falls back to public DNS (8.8.8.8) you get the public ELB A record. Two quick checks: 1) verify Route53 private hosted zone is associated with the VPC ID of eks-prod-3, 2) confirm resolver rules/forwarders aren't mis-prioritized.

katie: also check customer-facing NACLs / SGs on the nodes or the NAT gateway — we often see NACLs block UDP/53 to the VPC resolver or block the outbound to the in-VPC resolver IP. If the resolver is unreachable, fallback behavior explains intermittent public answers.

maria: Route53: private hosted zone ZONEID: Z123EXAMPLE is associated with VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d (should be the cluster VPC). I ran
```
$ aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --query 'HostedZones[?Id==`/hostedzone/Z123EXAMPLE`].{Name:Name}'
```
but need to double-check cross-account associations — customer said they moved some services between accounts.

alex: can you run from a failing pod: `dig @169.254.20.10 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example` and `dig @10.0.2.2 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example` and paste outputs?

maria: ran both:
```
$ dig @169.254.20.10 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example
10.2.5.18
$ dig @10.0.2.2 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example
; connection timed out.
$ dig @8.8.8.8 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example
54.210.33.12
```

maria: so node-local can answer using its cache, but it can't forward to VPC resolver (10.0.2.2). When cache misses it falls back to 8.8.8.8 and returns public IP.

rashid: probable root causes: resolver unreachable (NACL/SG/NAT), or AWS Route53 Resolver endpoint changed IP (if using outbound endpoints), or a route table change sending resolver traffic to a blackhole. Ask customer to confirm any recent VPC route / NACL / SG changes around 02:00 UTC.

katie: also check if there are any shared/private hosted zones with the same name in another account — if a private hosted zone exists in another VPC/account and has different records, DNS can be inconsistent if VPC associations are wrong. But your dig to 10.0.2.2 timing out is the main signal.

jordan: quick mitigation: add a node-local stub to always forward that domain to the in-VPC resolver IP explicitly and set `policy: fallthrough` disabled, or temporarily pin a static host entry in the pod (not ideal) — longer term restore connectivity to 10.0.2.2.

maria: customer says they recently applied a managed NACL change to tighten outbound 53 and accidentally allowed only TCP53, blocking UDP53. node-local uses UDP to talk to resolver.

alex: that fits. Action items:
- customer: re-open NACL to allow UDP/53 from node subnets -> 10.0.2.2 (and return traffic) (owner: AcmePay infra)
- customer: confirm VPC association of private hosted zone is vpc-0a1b2c3d (owner: AcmePay dns)
- support: add a temporary canary check to our health monitor to detect fallback-to-public answers for sensitive svc endpoints (owner: support)

maria: after they opened UDP/53 the node-local logs show successful forward. retest dig:
```
$ dig @10.0.2.2 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example
10.2.5.18
$ dig @8.8.8.8 +short svc.acmepay-internal.example
54.210.33.12
```

maria: curl from pod to service now returns expected cert and 200s. customer confirmed rollback of NACL change fixed it.

rashid: leaving note for postmortem: config change led to UDP53 blocked -> node-local fallback to public resolver -> intermittent public A records returned -> TLS cert mismatch + 503s. Recommend runbook update and a guardrail: alert when internal FQDN resolves to public IP.

deploy-bot: incident-note: ACME-2026-389999 - Root cause identified as NACL outbound UDP53 block; status: resolved; follow-ups: postmortem + monitoring. :white_check_mark:
